note: Replies to player letters. Tone is derived from trust, flame, town despair, social-web ties and any Blessing/Burden that surfaces. Slots: {fromName} {fromTown} {originTown} {quote} {neighbour} {neighbourTown}.

warm.title: A warm reply from {fromName}
openers: Dear friend, your letter found me on a good morning.
I read your letter aloud at the hearth. Twice.
echoes: You wrote "{quote}" and I could hear you saying it.
"{quote}" - that line has been in my pocket all day.
closers: Come by the road when you can. There is always a stool for you.
Write again. Your handwriting makes the mantel look kinder.

hopeful.title: A hopeful reply from {fromName}
openers: Thank you for writing. It arrived just when I needed a reason to find a pen.
Your letter came with the carrier's dust still on it, and I was glad of it.
echoes: About "{quote}": I have been turning it over, and I think you may be right.
You said "{quote}". I am not sure I believed it, but I would like to.
closers: Things are mending slowly here. Write again and tell me how it goes.

guarded.title: A careful reply from {fromName}
openers: Your letter arrived. I am not much for writing, so this will be short.
I did not know what to say, so I waited. Here is what I have.
echoes: You wrote "{quote}". Perhaps. I will think on it.
Regarding "{quote}": I have heard fine words before.
closers: If you mean it, the road runs both ways.
Send word again, if you like.

weary.title: A tired reply from {fromName}
openers: Forgive the shaky hand. The days here are long and the evenings longer.
I nearly did not answer. The ink had dried and so had most of me.
echoes: "{quote}" - it is kind of you to say. It is hard to hold on to, here.
You wrote "{quote}". I read it in the dark and it helped a little.
closers: Do not wait on me for a long letter. A short one from you would be enough.
Keep your own fire fed. Someone should.

bitter.title: A cold reply from {fromName}
openers: I will be brief. Letters are cheap, and this one is the cheapest I own.
Your letter reached me. I wish I could say that pleased me.
echoes: "{quote}" - easy to write from far away.
You wrote "{quote}". I have heard what that is worth.
closers: Do not expect much from me.

shortage: The granary at {fromTown} is thin and everyone counts loaves.
We are short on stores at {fromTown}; the caravans cannot come soon enough.
heavy: A quiet has settled over {fromTown}; people keep their doors shut.
{fromTown} feels hollow lately. The lamps go out early.
steady: {fromTown} is steady. Smoke from the chimneys again, which counts for something.
The hearth at {fromTown} burns without much fuss these days.

kin: {neighbour} is family, and asks after you.
friendship: {neighbour} says hello. We talk about you more than you would think.
{neighbour} and I shared your news over supper.
trade: {neighbour} says the road trade has been fair, and sends regards.
{neighbour} mentioned your name at the stall.
debt: {neighbour} and I are still settling an old debt, but I do not hold that against you.
{neighbour} is owed a favour by half the town, and I am not the only one.
rival: {neighbour} has not spoken to me in weeks. It colours everything.
I will not tell you what {neighbour} said. You would not like it.
struggling: I worry about {neighbour}, who is barely holding on. If you pass through, look in.
{neighbour} has gone very quiet. I fear for them.

postscript.blessing: P.S. Something small and good has happened. {line}
postscript.burden: P.S. I may as well say it. {line}
